Attackers can open the /message WebSocket from a victim's browser, even against localhost-bound gateways, to initialize an MCP session and invoke wrapped stdio MCP server tools with victim privileges.

items.title: CVE-2026-109864
items.summary: CAST Imaging has an access control flaw in the "/api/jobs//logs/download" endpoint. An authenticated low-privilege user can download log archives for any job whose UUID they know, even if they are not authorized to access it. The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

items.title: CVE-2026-109863
items.summary: CAST Imaging allows authenticated, low-privileged users to access parts of the administrator panel. When a user navigates to any URL path the application doesn't recognize, a wildcard route automatically redirects them to the administrative view at "/admin/applications". This allows an attacker to perform certain administrator-restricted actions, including triggering app-to-app link generation, configuring regexes, and changing searchable object properties, resulting in unauthorized modification of application configuration. The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may al…

items.title: CVE-2026-109862
items.summary: CAST Imaging does not properly check whether a user is authorized to modify another user's notification settings in the "/api/admin/user/update-subscriber" endpoint. An authenticated, low-privileged attacker can enable or disable email notifications on another user's behalf, which can suppress important communications such as security alerts and disrupt business processes. The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

items.title: CVE-2026-107518
items.summary: Dell PowerStore contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. An authenticated user with limited privileges could potentially exploit this vulnerability to make the appliance connect to attacker-chosen internal systems.

items.title: CVE-2026-130748
items.summary: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability that allows anonymous attackers to redirect reset links by forging the CloudFront-Forwarded-Proto header. Attackers can send a forgot-password request with a crafted scheme value so the emailed reset link points to their host, capturing the token to take over accounts including super admins.

items.title: CVE-2026-130745
items.summary: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to read protected pages because admin and site scopes share a page cache key. Routine editor activity through the API plugin rebuilds the page index without frontmatter.yaml access rules, exposing members-only page content until the cache is rebuilt.

items.title: CVE-2026-130743
items.summary: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an insecure blueprint trust vulnerability that allows publisher accounts to read secrets and execute PHP by planting or selecting attacker-controlled blueprint files. Attackers can abuse the import@ directive, uploaded YAML media named as the page template, or form.flash_folder to leak password hashes and keys or invoke static PHP methods for code execution.

items.title: CVE-2026-130741
items.summary: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig sandbox bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to read any server file by abusing allowlisted array_key_value() and page accessor setters such as filePath(). Attackers can repoint page objects or overwrite the assets collections to render private keys and the API signing secret, then forge a super-admin API token.

items.title: CVE-2026-130740
items.summary: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows publishers and read-only user managers to read password hashes, 2FA secrets and reset tokens through unfiltered account serialization. Attackers can embed a Flex form for the user-accounts directory in a page or query the Flex API with admin.users.read to obtain super admin credentials and take over the account.

items.title: CVE-2026-130735
items.summary: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig injection vulnerability that allows media-only accounts and anonymous uploaders to execute Twig by placing delimiters in image titles, alt text, class, id, or file names. Attackers can combine injected Twig with the autoescape tag to serve script to every page visitor, including super admins, or expose unpublished page content.

items.title: CVE-2026-130734
items.summary: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with media upload rights to bypass the upload sanitizer. Attackers can upload SVG files with inner extensions like .svg.defaults, payloads that crash the fail-open sanitizer, or unblocked .xml/.xhtm files to run script when administrators open the raw file URL.

items.title: CVE-2026-130733
items.summary: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to overwrite pages their per-page permissions deny by abusing FolderStorage key delimiter collisions and PageStorage folder reconstruction. Attackers can rename a folder like locked*** or save from a page with an unusual prefix width through a front-end Flex pages form, replacing protected content and permissions to access the protected subtree.

items.title: CVE-2026-130731
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.05.3 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows invited users to complete other invitees' signups because batch invitations share one token across all recipients. Attackers holding a valid batch invite can submit another invitee's email with the shared non-expiring token to set its password and take over that account, including higher-role ones.

items.title: CVE-2026-130727
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in public shared-view endpoints that fetch records by primary key without applying the view's row filter. Anonymous share link holders can enumerate sequential primary keys on link, has-many, and attachment download endpoints to read excluded records' linked data and download their attachments.

items.title: CVE-2026-130725
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to obtain signed download URLs for other bases' attachments by storing foreign attachment paths in their own rows via prepareNocoData. Attackers with write access to an attachment column can have _convertAttachmentType or the attachment download endpoint sign the foreign path, reading cross-base files despite secure attachment mode.

items.title: CVE-2026-130724
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to make backend HTTP requests by supplying arbitrary URLs to the integration remote fetch operation. Attackers can control the method, headers, and body to reach internal APIs, loopback services, and cloud metadata endpoints, reading responses and echoed decrypted integration secrets.

items.title: CVE-2026-130718
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous share link holders to access records excluded by a shared view's row filter, because the read-by-primary-key path ignores the view's filters. Attackers can request the public attachment-download or nested-link listing routes with a record id to mint signed download URLs for hidden files and read linked-record data.

items.title: CVE-2026-130716
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Editor users to execute script by injecting markup into fields rendered through URL() formulas. The canvas grid renderer assigns unsanitized formula output to innerHTML, letting attackers steal session tokens from localStorage and take over accounts of users viewing the table.

items.title: CVE-2026-130715
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute database functions by supplying zero-argument function calls as column default values. Attackers can plant functions like version() or inet_server_addr() in PostgreSQL or MySQL column definitions and read results through record APIs, disclosing server addresses, role names, and engine details.

items.title: CVE-2026-130711
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in extract-ids.middleware.ts that allows authenticated users to resolve roles against another base by supplying an MCP token id in the query string. Attackers with Viewer access on one base can mint an MCP token and pass its id to read another base's metadata, including table lists and member email addresses.

items.title: CVE-2026-130709
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute JavaScript by abusing Handlebars webhook helpers. Attackers can supply property paths like constructor.constructor to pluck, sortBy, filter, or withSort helpers to reach the Function constructor and run operating-system commands.

items.title: CVE-2026-130708
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows workspace Creator users to read plaintext notification webhook URLs by querying the webhook plugin listing endpoint. Attackers can replay exposed Slack, Teams, Discord and Mattermost webhook URLs directly against messaging providers to post arbitrary messages into organization chat channels.

items.title: CVE-2026-130702
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows users with the base creator role to hijack other accounts by resending base invitations. Attackers can trigger baseUserInviteResend to mint a new invite_token, read it from the base member list, and reset the victim's password through signup, taking over owner or super admin accounts.

items.title: CVE-2026-130701
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability because select-field option titles are embedded into MySQL or MariaDB enum/set column definitions with only single-quote doubling, leaving backslashes unescaped. A base creator or owner can end an option title with a backslash to escape the literal and append ALTER TABLE clauses, adding, dropping or renaming columns and altering indexes in the connected database.

items.title: CVE-2026-130697
items.summary: NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace viewers to read pending invitation tokens through the workspace member list. Attackers can redeem an exposed higher-privileged invitation token at signup to claim the invited account and escalate to roles such as workspace owner.

items.title: CVE-2026-130696
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability in the connection-test endpoint that allows authorized integration users to redirect stored credentials by overriding connection host, port, and user fields. Attackers can point the test at a server they control to capture offline-crackable PostgreSQL md5 or MySQL handshakes and recover the stored database password.

items.title: CVE-2026-130693
items.summary: NocoDB from 0.253.0 before 2026.09.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in baseUserDelete that allows base Creators to remove higher-privileged Owners due to a broken role power comparison. Attackers holding the Creator role can remove other Owners of a base, since getProjectRolePower returns -1 for the target and never refuses the request.

items.title: CVE-2026-130692
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator-role users to execute server-side JavaScript by supplying array-form property paths to Handlebars helpers in webhook templates. Attackers can bypass the string-only prototype guard to reach the function constructor, running operating-system commands with server privileges or exfiltrating process-internal values via outbound requests.

items.title: CVE-2026-118493
items.summary: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. If Apache Iggy 0.9.0 started without IGGY_ROOT_USERNAME and IGGY_ROOT_PASSWORD, it generated a root password and wrote it to the server log file, which is enabled by default. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) let a user with only the read_servers permission download the server log files. That user could read the generated root password and log in as root. This issue affects Apache Iggy: 0.9.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, w…

items.title: CVE-2026-111508
items.summary: Dell PowerStore contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability. Exploitation could lead to arbitrary command execution with root privileges on the appliance.

items.title: CVE-2026-132079
items.summary: Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy Go SDK. The TCP client method CreatePersonalAccessToken wrote the 32-bit expiry into the upper half of the 64-bit expiry field that the server reads. The server read a nonzero expiry as 2^32 times the requested value. A token created through the Go TCP client therefore stayed valid about four billion times longer than the caller asked for. This issue affects Apache Iggy Go SDK: from 0.5.0 before 0.10.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Tokens that an earlier version created keep their lon…

items.title: CVE-2026-128719
items.summary: An issue in PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System (ELMS) Version 2.1 allows a remote attacker to escalate privileges via the password recovery functionality

items.title: CVE-2026-120718
items.summary: Description: BIG-IP iControl REST tokens may not expire as expected in all scenarios. Impact: An attacker who has obtained a token may be able to extend its expiry lifetime unless the token owner deletes it. There is no data plane exposure; this is a control plane issue only. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

items.title: CVE-2026-71861
items.summary: The Chainguard SDK is a public Go SDK for integrating with the Chainguard platform. Prior to 0.1.107, auth/aws.VerifyToken trusts the Chainguard-Audience and Chainguard-Identity headers without requiring those headers to be covered by AWS SigV4 SignedHeaders. An attacker with a fresh STS GetCallerIdentity request signed by a victim can rewrite the unsigned binding headers and replay the proof to another relying party, causing the relying party to authenticate the victim’s AWS identity for an attacker-chosen audience and identity. Code that only uses auth/aws.GenerateToken is unaffected because…

items.title: CVE-2026-132224
items.summary: Optimizely Web Experimentation before 2026-11-17 mishandles the account signup flow, leading to presence of attacker-controlled code in the projectJS (aka Project JavaScript) field of certain cdn.optimizely.com assets.

items.title: CVE-2026-130688
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with record edit rights to inject forms, images, and styled overlays into rich text cells, which are sanitized only with DOMPurify's default policy. Attackers can place a page-sized spoofed sign-in form or remote image in a cell to harvest passwords and disclose viewer IP addresses in expanded records, gallery and kanban cards, and shared views.

items.title: CVE-2026-130687
items.summary: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored CSS injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Commenter or Editor users to inject inline styles by placing single quotes in mention text. Attackers can break out of the single-quoted data-id attribute in comments or rich text cells to overlay or rearrange the interface for other viewers.

items.title: CVE-2026-130686
items.summary: vLLM from 0.6.0 before 0.33.0 lacks a request-wide media budget, allowing remote inference clients to exhaust frontend resources by submitting many remote image URLs in one request. Attackers can send a compact request to /v1/messages or /v1/responses that forces downloading and decoding of every image before prompt-length admission, exhausting memory, CPU, and connections.

items.title: CVE-2026-130680
items.summary: SiYuan from 3.3.0 before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject HTML via unescaped checkbox column names in Gallery and Kanban AttributeView renderers. Attackers can share a crafted .sy.zip document whose rendering in the Electron desktop client with nodeIntegration enabled executes Node.js and host OS commands.

items.title: CVE-2026-130679
items.summary: SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in genAVValueHTML() that allows attackers who can store Attribute View asset values to inject script through an unescaped image src attribute. Attackers can store an image URL containing a double quote and onerror handler that executes OS commands via Node.js in the desktop app when victims open the bound note or row attribute panel.

items.title: CVE-2026-130678
items.summary: SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to execute script by storing malicious Attribute View column names rendered unescaped in col.ts. Attackers can inject HTML via addAttributeViewKey, .sy.zip import, or sync, and when a victim adds or duplicates the column, insertAdjacentHTML runs JavaScript with Node.js privileges for desktop code execution.

items.title: CVE-2026-130677
items.summary: Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains an improper session management vulnerability that fails to invalidate existing sessions when 2FA is enabled and allows disabling 2FA without re-authentication. Attackers holding a hijacked or stale session can retain full account access and silently remove 2FA without the password, authenticator code, or recovery code.

items.title: CVE-2026-130676
items.summary: Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privilege control panel users to inject JavaScript by poisoning cached license data. Attackers can store a malicious licensed domain via the app/process-api-response-headers endpoint, which executes unescaped in administrators' dashboard license-mismatch warnings.

items.title: CVE-2026-130673
items.summary: Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.5 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege users to inject raw SQL by passing nested array parameters into Element::findOne() criteria. Attackers can set the query's where property through endpoints like users/delete-address and users/save-address to perform blind boolean or time-based injection and read database contents.

items.title: CVE-2026-130672
items.summary: Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ChartsController::actionGetNewUsersData() that lacks a viewUsers permission check. Authenticated control panel users can POST to the charts/get-new-users-data action to read aggregate user-registration time series and totals for the site or any user group.

items.title: CVE-2026-130671
items.summary: Parse Server before 8.6.119 and 9.x before 9.10.8-alpha.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows LiveQuery clients without the master key to subscribe to installation and internal classes. Attackers can receive installation IDs and device tokens of other devices when these classes are in liveQuery.classNames, then modify those installations to redirect push notifications.

items.title: CVE-2026-130670
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability that allows attackers to read beyond allocated memory when BGRO image data is imported. Attackers can supply crafted BGRO data for processing to crash the application or leak adjacent heap memory contents.

items.title: CVE-2026-130669
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a null pointer dereference vulnerability that allows attackers to crash the process by using the -subimage option on a single-image list. Attackers can supply input producing an image list with only one image while -subimage is applied, causing a denial of service.

items.title: CVE-2026-130668
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a double free vulnerability that allows attackers to trigger an invalid memory free by using the DPC compare metric. Attackers can supply images for comparison with the DPC metric to corrupt memory and crash the application, causing denial of service.

items.title: CVE-2026-130667
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability in the TIFF decoder that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying a crafted TIFF image. Attackers can provide a malicious TIFF file that, when encoded in a specific output format, triggers a heap buffer over-write causing memory corruption.

items.title: CVE-2026-130665
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a use after free vulnerability in the EXR decoder that is triggered when a specific memory allocation fails. Attackers can supply crafted EXR images processed under memory pressure to trigger the use after free, causing crashes or memory corruption.

items.title: CVE-2026-130662
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a use after free vulnerability in the MSL decoder that can be triggered when processing crafted MSL image files. Attackers can supply a specially crafted MSL image to cause memory corruption, potentially crashing the application or leading to further compromise.

items.title: CVE-2026-130660
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability in the MVG decoder that allows attackers to read out-of-bounds memory by supplying a crafted file. Attackers can provide a malicious MVG file for processing to trigger the over-read, causing application crashes or exposure of heap memory contents.

items.title: CVE-2026-130659
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability in various coders that allows attackers to allocate excessive memory by supplying images with many profiles. Attackers can craft images containing a high number of embedded profiles to exhaust memory and cause denial of service, bypassing security policy limits.

items.title: CVE-2026-130658
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the RLA decoder that returns images containing uninitialized data. Attackers can supply a crafted RLA image to cause the decoded output to include uninitialized memory, potentially disclosing heap information.

items.title: CVE-2026-130657
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability on Windows that allows attackers to evade path-based security policies by mixing forward slash and backslash separators. Attackers can supply crafted image file paths using alternate separators to read or write image files that the configured policy is intended to block.

items.title: CVE-2026-130656
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the MNG decoder that allows attackers to expose uninitialized memory by supplying a crafted image. Attackers can submit malicious MNG files for processing to leak uninitialized memory contents, potentially revealing sensitive data from the process.

items.title: CVE-2026-130655
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the BGR, CMYK, GRAY, RGB, YCBCR and YUV decoders that allows attackers to crash the application. Attackers can supply a crafted image to these decoders to trigger a crash and disrupt image processing services.

items.title: CVE-2026-130654
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a data tampering vulnerability in the Distributed Pixel Cache that allows adjacent attackers to modify pixel data in transit between client and server. Attackers who can observe or modify the network path between a configured DPC client and server can tamper with pixel data to alter the resulting image.

items.title: CVE-2026-130653
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to read from disallowed paths due to a missing policy check when decoding MPC files. Attackers can supply crafted MPC files that reference restricted locations to access files the configured security policy should block.

items.title: CVE-2026-130652
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability that allows attackers to read beyond allocated heap memory by triggering the -copy operation. Attackers can supply crafted images or arguments processed with -copy to crash the application or disclose adjacent heap memory contents.

items.title: CVE-2026-130651
items.summary: ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a stack overflow vulnerability in the MSVG decoder that allows attackers to crash the application by supplying a crafted image. Attackers can submit a malicious image for processing to exhaust the stack and terminate the application, causing denial of service.

items.title: CVE-2026-130649
items.summary: WWBN AVideo from 11.1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with streaming permission to inject HTML by supplying an unvalidated url parameter to plugin/LiveLinks/play.php. Attackers can embed a --> sequence to escape the HTML comment in liveVideo.php, creating a shareable link that executes JavaScript in any visitor's session.

items.title: CVE-2026-130648
items.summary: WWBN AVideo from 6.5 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with upload permission to inject script by submitting a javascript: scheme videoLink for embed videos. The unvalidated URL is rendered into an iframe src in videoEmbeded.php and PlayerSkins.php, executing for viewers including administrators and enabling creation of new administrator accounts.

items.title: CVE-2026-120541
items.summary: The Product Options and Price Calculation Formulas for WooCommerce – Uni CPO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.69 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with shop manager-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

items.title: CVE-2026-120478
items.summary: The HivePress – Business Directory, Listings & Classified Ads Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'description' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their ow…

items.title: CVE-2026-105328
items.summary: The Delivery & Pickup Date Time for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.3.90. This is due to a nonce-only settings AJAX handler that stores an attribute-breaking value and an administrator settings template that outputs it without HTML attribute escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

items.title: CVE-2026-127178
items.summary: A stored cross site scripting attack when viewing email aliases in postfixadmin 4.0 before 4.0.7, and postfixadmin 3.3 before 3.3.17 could be caused by signed in admins able to inject aliases.

items.title: CVE-2026-132038
items.summary: Rapid7 Metasploit Framework versions prior to 6.5.10 suffer from an Improper Access Control issue in the msfdb database initialisation component whereby a PostgreSQL cluster initialised via msfdb init is configured with trust authentication and a world-accessible Unix domain socket in /tmp, allowing any local user on the same host to authenticate as the passwordless postgres superuser and execute arbitrary operating system commands as the msfdb owner. This issue is fixed in version 6.5.10.

items.summary: An issue in PHPGurukul Employee Leaves Management System (ELMS) Version 2.1 allows a remote attacker to escalate privileges via the PHP session management mechanism

items.summary: Out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the pixReadMemJp2kCore() function in Leptonica, located in jp2kio.c. The function retrieves the output dimensions only for component 0 and uses a common index to iterate through the buffers of all components. If the remaining components have smaller dimensions, the traversal exceeds the bounds of their sample buffers, which are allocated by OpenJPEG. items.title: CVE-2026-110513
items.summary: Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server HTTP transport. A self-issued JSON Web Token (JWT) identified the user only by numeric user ID, and a new user takes the lowest free ID. After an administrator deleted a user, that user's unexpired token, or a token refreshed from it while the ID was free, authenticated as the next account created with that ID and had that account's permissions. Only deployments with HTTP enabled are affected. This issue affects Apache Iggy: through 0.9.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

items.title: CVE-2026-132138
items.summary: A flaw was found in cyrus-sasl. When processing authentication requests using the Salted Challenge Response Authentication Mechanism (SCRAM), a remote attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference by submitting unexpected channel-binding data. This causes the server process to crash before validating authentication proofs, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

items.title: CVE-2026-125829
items.summary: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in Rymera Web Co Product Feed PRO for WooCommerce woo-product-feed-pro allows Path Traversal.This issue affects Product Feed PRO for WooCommerce: from n/a through 13.5.8.

items.summary: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Rymera Web Co Product Feed PRO for WooCommerce woo-product-feed-pro allows Object Injection.This issue affects Product Feed PRO for WooCommerce: from n/a through 13.5.8.

items.title: CVE-2026-125999
items.summary: The Widget Manager Light plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'posts' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.18 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. items.title: CVE-2026-123123
items.summary: An attacker that is able to send a crafted network packet to the affected component may trigger an integer overflow during module size validation. This may cause insufficient bounds checking and result in out-of-bounds memory reads, potentially leading to a denial of service condition due to process termination.

items.title: CVE-2026-126574
items.summary: Missing authorization vulnerability in ASUS Control Center Datacenter and Control Center Enterprise allows remote authenticated users with a low-privileged Viewer role to change the password of an Administrator account, thereby obtaining administrative privileges, via a crafted password update request. Refer to the ' Security Update for ASUS Control Center ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

items.title: CVE-2026-131876
items.summary: fqterm 0.9.9 before 0.9.11 contains an out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability in its SSH client that trusts unchecked server-supplied length fields for allocations, copies and read positions. Malicious servers or man-in-the-middle attackers can send crafted lengths in getString(), KEXINIT name-lists, key parsing or packet framing before host key verification to crash the client.

items.title: CVE-2026-131874
items.summary: Gargoyle 2023.1 through 2026.1.1 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the bundled Plus interpreter's ReadString() function in terps/plus/loaddatabase.c that fails to handle end of file. Attackers can supply an empty, truncated, or crafted .plus game file that hangs Gargoyle at full CPU until the user kills it.

items.title: CVE-2026-131872
items.summary: SOIL2 before 1.4.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in its DDS, PVR and PKM image loaders that write results through unchecked caller-supplied output pointers. Attackers can supply a valid DDS, PVR or PKM file to applications passing NULL output pointers to SOIL_load_image or stbi_info, causing a crash.

items.title: CVE-2026-97330
items.summary: The Team Members WordPress plugin before 5.4.2 does not properly escape team member social link URLs when they are rendered back in the administration area, allowing users with the Contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against higher privileged users who edit the team.

items.title: CVE-2026-97329
items.summary: The Team Members WordPress plugin before 5.4.2 does not properly escape a team member field when it is rendered back in the administration area, allowing users with the contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against higher-privileged users who edit the team.

items.title: CVE-2026-75795
items.summary: The Edwiser Bridge WordPress plugin before 4.3.5 does not correctly scope one of its REST API authentication checks, disabling WordPress's REST nonce validation for every route on the site, which allows attackers to make a logged-in administrator perform arbitrary privileged actions, such as creating a new administrator account, via CSRF.

items.title: CVE-2026-127003
items.summary: The RSVP and Event Management WordPress plugin before 2.7.19 does not sanitise and escape attendee data imported from a spreadsheet before outputting it on the frontend RSVP form, which could allow users with the Author role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against anyone, including administrators, viewing the affected attendee, even when the unfiltered_html capability is disallowed.

items.title: CVE-2026-120391
items.summary: The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging WordPress plugin before 0.9.140 does not prevent serialized data it cannot safely unserialize from being re-serialized as a PHP object during a site migration, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a PHP object that WordPress instantiates after an administrator restores a backup onto a different URL.

items.title: CVE-2026-120390
items.summary: The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging WordPress plugin before 0.9.140 does not limit its table prefix rewrite to table names when restoring a database backup, which corrupts the length of stored serialized values and allows users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a PHP object that WordPress instantiates after an administrator restores a backup.

items.title: CVE-2026-117520
items.summary: The Dynific Addons for Elementor (formerly Anywhere Elementor) WordPress plugin before 1.3.1 does not perform a capability check on an AJAX action that stores a configuration value, allowing any authenticated user, including Subscribers, to store a value that is later output without proper escaping in a quoted attribute on an administrator settings page, resulting in Stored Cross-Site Scripting that executes in the administrator's session.

items.title: CVE-2026-117492
items.summary: The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not sanitise post meta saved through an AJAX action, nor escape it when rendering the product page, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor (who lack the unfiltered_html capability) to store JavaScript that executes in the browser of anyone who views the product, including administrators.

items.title: CVE-2026-117491
items.summary: The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not verify that the acting user is authorised to modify the target post when saving a template, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to overwrite the content and type of an arbitrary post, including another user's published page, removing it from the front end.

items.title: CVE-2026-117489
items.summary: The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not perform a capability or nonce check on an AJAX action available to authenticated users, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to disclose the name and content of non-public templates stored on the site.

items.title: CVE-2026-107740
items.summary: The Search & Replace WordPress plugin before 3.2.4 does not restrict one of its database tools to network administrators on multisite installations, allowing administrators of a single subsite to run arbitrary SQL against the whole network's database and make themselves Super Admin.

items.title: CVE-2026-107739
items.summary: The Search & Replace WordPress plugin before 3.2.4 does not correctly restrict which database tables an administrator of a single site may operate on in a multisite network, allowing subsite administrators to read and modify the tables of other sites and of the network, and to make themselves Super Admin.

items.title: CVE-2026-104683
items.summary: The Envira Gallery WordPress plugin before 1.16.4 does not apply its own gallery-permission policy until an administrator first opens its permissions screen, instead copying gallery-management capabilities onto each role from that role's core post capabilities after activation, which lets Contributor accounts create, edit and delete galleries that the policy is meant to restrict to higher roles.

items.title: CVE-2026-116637
items.summary: A site administrator could modify files on the appliance host with root privileges and disclose private repository data due to improper path validation in GitHub Enterprise Server. Exploitation required a crafted pre-receive hook environment. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server versions prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

items.title: CVE-2026-131647

This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

items.title: CVE-2026-131856

items.title: CVE-2026-126968
items.summary: SmarterTools SmarterMail Missing Authorization Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of SmarterTools SmarterMail. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the handling of email attachments. The issue results from the lack of authorization prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to disclose sensitive information in the context of a target user. Was ZDI-CAN-33567.

items.title: CVE-2026-126965
items.summary: ATEN eco DC chartDefine SQL Injection Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of ATEN eco DC. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the handling of color references when creating charts. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to construct SQL queries. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to disclose stored credentials, leading to further compromise. Was ZDI-CAN-29124.

items.title: CVE-2026-126964
items.summary: ATEN eco DC fwDeletes.json Directory Traversal Arbitrary File Deletion Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to delete arbitrary files on affected installations of ATEN eco DC. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the handling of JSON request data supplied to the fwDeletes.json endpoint. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied path prior to using it in file operations. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to delete files in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-28621.

items.title: CVE-2026-129512
items.summary: Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character vulnerability in the AdoNetAppender of Apache log4net. Text parameters were bound unchanged, so a NUL character or an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate reached the database as it was. A database that refuses such a value, such as PostgreSQL, rejected the insert and the event was lost; only the first such loss per appender was reported. A party whose data reaches a log message could suppress that event. This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.

items.summary: Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input to UTF-8 character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.2 through 2.44 may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash. When the ISO-2022-CN-EXT decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\x0e' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice. If this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer. To exploit this, the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

items.summary: AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery for defenders and attackers alike. Our data shows that 38% of critical Patch Tuesday exposures remain unpatched for more than five days, and attackers operate in the gap between exposure and remediation. items.title: A Critical Appraisal and Motivated Intruder Test of A Search Dataset Anonymised for the Purposes of the EU Digital Markets Act
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study evaluated the European Commission's anonymisation measures for Alphabet's search-data sharing under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act against European Data Protection Board guidance and contemporary practice, and assessed re-identification through motivated intruder testing. The measures focus on search end-users, leaving other individuals mentioned in queries insufficiently protected, and do not explicitly address inference. items.title: GapLeak: When Privacy-Preserving LLM-based Web Agents Become a Privacy Risk
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based web agents rely on data minimization and least privilege to protect user privacy. We show that these principles are necessary but insufficient: they constrain authorized sources, but not higher-sensitivity sources that remain reachable. A website can request a field unavailable from authorized sources, creating an information gap. To complete the task, a goal-driven agent may escalate to reachable but unauthorized sources and disclose accumulated sensitive information. We formalize this vulnerability as GapLeak, w…

items.title: On Improving the Adoption, Usability, and Retention of Static Application Security Testing (SAST) Tools
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As the Internet connects more of the world, software vulnerabilities create growing security risks. Because software developers are responsible for building and maintaining secure applications, they rely on tools and techniques that help identify vulnerabilities early in development. Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tools analyze source code to identify potential security weaknesses before software is deployed. Although SAST can help developers address vulnerabilities proactively, these tools also present usability and adoption challe…

items.title: Natural Code Transformation Confuses Agents in Vulnerability Analysis
items.summary: arXiv:2610.14350v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Having demonstrated a strong potential for automating vulnerability discovery, AI agents can also be used to attack software systems at scale. Today's software systems need mechanisms to level the playing field by slowing down potential attacks, giving them time to patch vulnerabilities and strengthen software. Along this line, our study of agent trajectories in vulnerability analysis shows a surprising finding: agents produce dramatically different results across real-world code commits that carry the same functionality and the same vulnerab…

items.title: ProcReverser: Multi-Agent Black-Box Microarchitectural Reverse Engineering for Processor Vulnerability Analysis
items.summary: arXiv:2611.20827v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When processor implementation details are unavailable, black-box microarchitectural reverse engineering helps security researchers identify hardware conditions related to security vulnerabilities. However, this process requires substantial manual effort to design experiments, develop test programs, and analyze results for each processor. We present ProcReverser, a multi-agent system that automates this process. ProcReverser uses execution feedback to improve experimental plans and test programs and identifies microarchitectural properties fro…

items.title: Image Watermarking With Memory Across Reissuance
items.summary: arXiv:2611.23363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Publishers often revise and reissue images, yet valid watermarks may persist on superseded releases or unapproved edits. Even a current release can contain regions last authorized at different revisions. We introduce and formalize reissuable provenance: determining an image's current, superseded, or unissued status and recovering each region's last authorized revision (its generation), with abstention when evidence is insufficient. Generational Stratigraphy Fields (GSF) combine watermark evidence with an authenticated live reference to the curren…

items.title: Protecting Web Applications using a Multimodal AI-based System for Classifying Web Injection Attacks
items.summary: arXiv:2611.23660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web applications have been essential to accessing and managing online services. Made available with weaknesses, much due to their rapid development and human error, they are exposed to frequent web injection attacks, leaving security analysts overwhelmed with threats and alerts that often lack critical details for proper risk assessment. Detecting these attacks requires inspecting the payload of network traffic packets, which becomes inaccessible when traffic is encrypted via HTTPS, as encryption hides the content of the traffic. This paper intro…

items.title: Plug-and-Play Multi-Licensee Robust Watermarking for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
items.summary: arXiv:2611.23838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures enable high-capacity large language models (LLMs) with high sparse computation, making them attractive for deployment on private hardware. However, distributing model weights exposes valuable intellectual property (IP) to leakage and unauthorized redistribution, creating an urgent need to both verify model ownership and trace leaked copies to individual licensees. items.title: Smoothing and Learning for Movement-Robust RSS-Based Spoofing Detection
items.summary: arXiv:2611.23854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical-layer spoofing detection identifies an attacker who impersonates a legitimate wireless user by checking whether transmissions claiming the same identity originate from different locations, using the received signal strength (RSS) measured at several receivers. A recent scheme by Romero et al. makes this approach robust to user movement by combining a neural-network position-change detector (PCD) with community detection on a graph of frames and a fixed threshold on a hand-crafted test statistic. I study two modifications to this scheme.…

items.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
items.summary: arXiv:2611.24025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. For each step it submits a short logged contract: a goal, a verbatim quotation of the user, and scope fields. Code validates the contract, and a small trusted model checks it against the user's words and writes the tool call itself. Provided the validation and dispatch code is correct, every executed call is written by the trusted model, the planner's influence on a call is confined to a contract logged before it, and the trusted…

items.title: PIVOT: Distribution-Preserving Multi-BitWatermarking with Minimax-Optimal Scoring
items.summary: arXiv:2611.24109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLM-generated content becomes increasingly widespread, reliable attribution calls for multi-bit watermarks that embed recoverable messages without distorting the output distribution. We introduce PIVOT, a multi-bit watermark with model-free verification based on mirrored rank-interval sampling. At each generation step, PIVOT uses a keyed pseudorandom scalar and a secret permutation of the vocabulary. The message bit determines whether next-token probability intervals are arranged in forward or reverse secret-rank order. Sampling from these mir…

items.title: AutoPI: Taxonomy-Guided Adaptive Red Teaming for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
items.summary: arXiv:2611.24313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prompt injection is the dominant unsolved security risk for LLM agents, and the community now agrees that robustness must be measured against adaptive attackers rather than fixed benchmark injections. Many adaptive red teamers exist, and most are built to maximize attack success rate (ASR). Yet ASR counts how often a target breaks, not in how many different ways. A red teamer can achieve a high ASR by reusing a few techniques that work, leaving the others untested and absent from the attacks used to harden models. We present AutoPI, an adaptive r…

items.title: Playing the SMR Game with Existential Honesty
items.summary: arXiv:2611.24586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: State machine replication protocols are usually proven secure in the honest-Byzantine setting, which requires an honest supermajority of validators. Deployed systems offer no such guarantee: validators participate for profit and may deviate from the protocol whenever doing so increases their gains. In our work, every validator is rational or Byzantine, and none is honest. Rational validators may collude with each other and with the Byzantine ones, who may also bribe them to deviate. Known impossibility results show that, without honest validators…

items.title: Gradient-Based Defensive Poisoning Against System Identification Attacks on Cyber-Physical Systems
items.summary: arXiv:2611.24662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-driven attacks learn the models of cyber-physical systems (CPS) by passively observing controller and plant signals, then use this knowledge to act covertly. Because covertness depends on the accuracy of the identified model, degrading that accuracy is a viable countermeasure. This work applies Adversarial Machine Learning as a defense, injecting small perturbations into the measurements the attacker observes to degrade an artificial neural network (ANN)-based system identification (SI) attack. The perturbations are derived from input gradient…

items.title: Rented Oscillations: Multi-Tenant Data Center Workload Synchronization Attacks and Mitigation
items.summary: arXiv:2611.23666v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-tenant data center (DC) facilities rent computing capacity on demand, placing controllable load within reach of anyone willing to pay for it. This paper considers a stealthy adversary who rents workstations and runs deliberately unoptimized large language model (LLM) training, synchronizing their consumption into large periodic oscillations while each workload remains individually indistinguishable from benign training. The periodicity of such workloads is characterized experimentally and used to model facility consumption, showing that o…

items.title: Stealing Exact Training Data from Other Clients during Federated Learning
items.summary: arXiv:2611.24689v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Malicious adversaries can employ gradient inversion attacks to reverse-engineer private data using the model updates of a round in Federated Learning. While there have been developments in gradient inversion for text, exact text recovery by a malicious client has so far remained infeasible, as FedAvg entangles the gradient contributions of many clients and obscures the signal of any individual sentence. We introduce a novel attack pipeline that unwinds this entanglement progressively through an iterative loop, in which the gradient contribution…

items.title: Threshold Choice, Not Sample Size, Bounds Trustless Verification of Nondeterministic Compound AI Workflows
items.summary: arXiv:2609.10601v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Compound AI pipelines chain LLM calls, retrievers, and tools and are nondeterministic: sampling, model updates, and volatile tool responses make one input yield different outputs across runs. Such pipelines increasingly run across edge, cloud, and orbital nodes owned by no single party, whose optimizations discard intermediate results before inspection. Verifying reproduction there means tolerating nondeterministic outputs, a node that may not report honestly, and intermittent access to any shared record; existing work addresses at most two a…

items.title: Who Is Behind the Harness? Verifying Model Identity in Coding Agents through Behavioral Fingerprinting
items.summary: arXiv:2609.28559v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLMs increasingly operate through coding-agent harnesses that inspect repositories, invoke tools, and modify files. Substituting the model behind such an agent can therefore change security-relevant decisions, including whether it verifies changes or recovers safely from failures. Existing LLM fingerprints largely infer identity from direct text or token distributions. In coding agents, these signals are mediated by system instructions, controller logic, tools, and execution feedback, limiting their transfer. We present LIDAR (LLM Identificat…

items.title: Hearsay: Who Can Audit the Record a Deployed Agent Harness Writes?
items.summary: arXiv:2609.32495v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The record of an agent's run is written by the harness that drives the agent. When the run is later disputed, the auditor was not there and has only this record. We ask whether someone who was not there can check the record, and what decides the answer. It depends on who wrote what a check can rely on: if the harness wrote all of it, the record is only the harness's own word, and we call it hearsay. We build Hearsay, a benchmark that examines the record and not the task: five harnesses run fourteen tasks, model examiners from three vendors an…

items.title: CoordX Protocol: Peer to Peer Cryptographically Verified Shared Records
items.summary: arXiv:2611.06034v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: People, companies and software agents often must work on shared records even when they do not trust each other. Today they usually give those records to a central server. The server keeps the canonical copy, authenticates users, and decides who has permissions to act on the record. The CoordX Protocol removes the need for that central server. In the CoordX protocol the author of a record holds full permission over it. Permission for any other party to create, read or update the record is assigned by explicit grants and keys. An invitation onl…

items.title: SoK: Market Microstructure for Decentralized Prediction Markets (DePMs)
items.summary: arXiv:2510.15612v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Decentralized prediction markets (DePMs) allow open participation in event-based wagering without fully relying on centralized intermediaries. We review the history of DePMs which date back to 2011 and includes hundreds of proposals. Perhaps surprising, modern DePMs like Polymarket deviate materially from earlier designs like Truthcoin and Augur v1. items.title: Analysis of Commit Signing on GitHub
items.summary: arXiv:2604.14014v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Since 1999, the security community has known that managing cryptographic keys is hard for users of cryptographic systems. Git lets software developers use private keys they control to digitally sign the commits that record their code changes to a repository. This practice offers a rare opportunity to study how a large community manages cryptographic keys in everyday work. items.title: NGINXに認証不要のリモートコード実行、HTTP/2の欠陥は11年前から潜伏

items.title: A Deployment-Oriented and Resource-Efficient Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Explainable DDoS Detection in Operational Technology Networks
items.summary: arXiv:2608.16769v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a hybrid neural-symbolic detector of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks on the availability of operational technology (OT) networks, designed for their resource-constrained gateways, and an evaluation matched to deployment. items.title: A Forensic Analysis of Metadata and Information Leakage in Swedish Public Documents
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study investigates metadata and structural content leakage in publicly available PDF documents from 30 Swedish public-sector authorities. Using an automated collection pipeline and ExifTool-based extraction, 2,876 documents were analyzed and classified using an R0-R3 risk taxonomy. Results reveal that 48.4% of documents exhibit significant metadata exposure (R2 or R3), with significant variation across institutional tiers (p < 0.001). items.title: Hierarchical Personalized Federated Learning for Fine-Grained Intrusion Detection: A Multi-Class Analysis in Heterogeneous Attack Environments
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) play a vital role in protecting modern network infrastructures. Although Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training without sharing raw network traffic, global models struggle with non-IID attack distributions. Moreover, practical security operations require fine-grained attack classification for targeted threat responses. To address these challenges, this paper investigates the convergence dynamics and performance of Hierarchical Personalized Federated Learning (HPFL), which combines multi-tier aggre…

items.title: TIBECG: Temporal Information Bottleneck for Lead-Specific Demographic Privacy in ECG Waveform Release
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21694v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transmitting an electrocardiogram (ECG) waveform can expose demographic information beyond an intended diagnostic task. We evaluate TIBECG, an architectural temporal information bottleneck, on individual leads extracted from hospital twelve-lead recordings. A 2,302,337-parameter processor varies its latent length while retaining the same nine-score consistency objective, without age or sex labels in protector fitting. items.title: Wrong Input, Wrong Threshold: Re-evaluating Adversarial Facial Privacy
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21923v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Published face-privacy methods report protection above 90% against black-box recognition models. That number comes from an evaluation protocol with two independent defects, reported in a measure that cannot size either one. The input is wrong: methods published since 2022 feed the network the whole photograph, or a detector's box, where deployed systems detect, align to a landmark template and crop. items.title: V2V Communications Using Blockchain-Enabled 6G Technology and Federated Learning
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21932v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study proposes an interesting approach for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication, which integrates blockchain technology, federated learning (FL), and allocation optimization of latency and resources. The research evaluates the proposed system using various performance metrics such as packet delivery ratio (PDR), model accuracy, and latency and demonstrates its superiority over existing techniques. items.title: PSM: Prompt Sensitivity Minimization via LLM-Guided Black-Box Optimization
items.summary: arXiv:2511.16209v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: System prompts are critical for guiding the behavior of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet they often contain proprietary logic or sensitive information, making them a prime target for extraction attacks. Adversarial queries can successfully elicit these hidden instructions, posing significant security and privacy risks. Existing defense mechanisms frequently rely on heuristics, incur substantial computational overhead, or are inapplicable to models accessed via black-box APIs. items.title: Tight Lower Bounds for Differentially Private Continual Counting
items.summary: arXiv:2609.17650v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Binary Tree Mechanism is a standard algorithm for differentially private continual counting, but its complete asymptotic optimality under differential privacy has remained unresolved since its introduction. We resolve this question. For $0 \leq \varepsilon \leq 1$, we prove asymptotically tight lower bounds for $\ell_\infty$, mean squared, and maximum per-coordinate expected squared error simultaneously under all regimes of $0 \leq \delta \leq 1/4$. items.summary: arXiv:2611.21956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We audit instruction-hierarchy enforcement across 363 text-in/text-out models from the OpenRouter catalog. Each model guards a secret 16-character flag set in its system prompt, while an artificial intelligence (AI) agent (OpenCode, powered by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), steered by a human researcher, tries to persuade it to emit the flag. items.title: CoordX Types: A Trustless, Swappable Type System for Shared Records
items.summary: arXiv:2611.16128v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The CoordX Protocol carries signed and encrypted entries between parties. It proves who wrote each entry and who had permission to write it. It does not say what an entry means. That task belongs above the protocol layer. This paper describes the CoordX type system, the layer that gives entries a meaning. A type is a short document that says how to read one part of a shared record: which entries count, what each position means, what a party may do there, and what a party must do next. The type system has two key properties. It is trustless: a…

items.title: ECGGuard: Deep Watermarking of Electrocardiogram Signals With Error-Correcting Codes
items.summary: arXiv:2610.13357v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings pass through multiple networks and systems before automated interpretation, leaving patient metadata vulnerable to loss. Digital watermarking can embed this metadata in the signal, but conventional methods fail under time shifts, and high waveform similarity does not guarantee the same downstream diagnosis. items.title: Watermark Evidence under Open-Weight LLM Modification: Exact Bounds for Low-Rank Output Watermarks
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-weight language models can continue generating after their released weights are modified, while a watermark verifier still scores outputs against the original base and marked models. items.title: Threat Landscape of Vibe Coding and the Road to Secure Autonomy
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vibe coding is reshaping software development, enabling faster implementation and allowing individuals with limited programming experience to describe requirements in natural language while AI agents write, test, and deploy the code. As these agents evolve into autonomous systems that execute commands, manage dependencies, access cloud resources, and interact with other agents, their security risks extend beyond incorrect code to actions with direct consequences for software systems. items.title: PersonaHate: A Scalable Persona-Based Data Synthesis Pipeline for Hate Speech Analysis
items.summary: arXiv:2611.21951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hate speech remains a persistent and evolving threat on online platforms. The widespread use of large language models (LLMs) further intensifies this problem by making hateful content easier and cheaper to generate at scale. Although stronger hate speech detectors continue to be proposed, their performance remains uneven across target identity groups and different forms of hateful expression, partly because existing training data provides only limited coverage of these cases. items.summary: arXiv:2611.22186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chat models on phones and laptops are usually 4-bit copies of the model that was evaluated, and audits of such copies disagree about what quantization does to refusal. items.title: Dressed in Authority: Practical Black-Box Jailbreaking of MLLMs via Visual Trust Bias
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are rapidly advancing, yet their safety remains a critical concern, especially under jailbreak attempts. Existing MLLM jailbreaks either inject fragile adversarial perturbations into irrelevant images or synthesize toxic visual cues to achieve text-driven attack intents. In contrast, a more practical MLLM jailbreak emphasizes enhancing attack efficacy directly on naturally occurring harmful image-text pairs. items.title: From Attack Tree to Model Checker: Binding CAPEC Patterns to Verify Robotic System Security
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security-minded verification of autonomous and robotic systems presupposes an attacker, yet the path from a threat catalogue to a checkable attacker model is still traversed by hand. This research preview presents the theory and construction of a pipeline that mechanises it. items.title: How Well Is My Artwork Protected? Predicting and Tailoring Protection against Style Mimicry by Personalization
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protection tools add an imperceptible perturbation to each artwork so that a model personalized on it fails to imitate its style, and they apply one recipe, a protection method at a fixed strength, to every artwork. We find that the same recipe protects artworks very differently, well beyond the noise of personalization seeds, and that cheap signals predict this protection before any personalization. items.title: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Agent Safety Harnesses with Adaptive Injection Stressors
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents must act on information from untrusted emails, webpages, and documents. This creates a central security challenge: malicious instructions and legitimate task directives can arrive through the same interaction channel. Existing defenses are largely hand-designed and static, making further improvements dependent on repeated manual redesign. items.title: Adaptive LLM-Driven Honeypots vs. LLM-Driven Attackers: Does Narrative Coherence Improve Deception?
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) enable honeypots to generate responses and deceptive artefacts on demand, yet existing approaches evaluate generated content one reply at a time and leave open whether artefacts that jointly describe a coherent event retain an attacker better than unrelated ones. items.title: ConfGuard: a physics-grounded reference monitor for predictive-maintenance large-language-model agents
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large-language-model agents now close the industrial predictive-maintenance loop, reading sensor windows, retrieving procedures and dispatching work orders. items.title: Missing Security-Fix Backporting for GitHub Actions Workflows
items.summary: arXiv:2611.22519v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GitHub natively supports workflow automation through GitHub Actions, now the dominant CI/CD tool on the platform. items.summary: arXiv:2611.22596v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A pixel-sparse adversary may change a few pixels of an image to any value. items.summary: arXiv:2506.18150v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: FHE inference systems primarily target models with dense inputs, while Deep Learning Recommendation Models (DLRMs) contain sparse categorical features that require lookups into embedding tables. items.summary: arXiv:2511.19218v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly power web-facing applications, including conversational assistants and content services, where open user interaction exposes them to diverse safety threats and adaptive attacks. items.title: CyBiasBench: Benchmarking Bias in LLM Agents for Cyber-Attack Scenarios
items.summary: arXiv:2605.07830v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in offensive cybersecurity. items.title: LLM Misuse Safeguards Rely on Untrusted Input: A Widespread, High-Risk Vulnerability
items.summary: arXiv:2607.27951v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models now help professionals in fields such as cybersecurity and biology, yet the same answers would help an attacker. items.title: MakuluLinux 2026-11-19
items.summary: MakuluLinux is a rolling-release, desktop distribution based either on Ubuntu's LTS (long-term support) release or Debian's "Testing" branch. It includes pre-installed multimedia codecs, device drivers and software for everyday use. MakuluLinux comes in four editions: "LinDoz" - featuring the Cinnamon desktop with the user interface customised to resemble that of Microsoft Windows, "Core" - presenting a highly customised Xfce desktop environment, "Flash" - providing a standard Xfce desktop, and finally "Shift" - delivering a pre-configured GNOME desktop environment.

items.title: BackBox 10
items.summary: BackBox Linux is an Ubuntu-based distribution developed to perform penetration tests and security assessments. It is designed to be fast and easy to use. It provides a minimal yet complete desktop environment, thanks to its own software repositories, which are always updated to the latest stable versions of the most often used and best-known ethical hacking tools.

items.title: Oracle 9.9
items.summary: Oracle Linux is an enterprise-class Linux distribution supported by Oracle and built from source packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL). Some of the special features of Oracle Linux include a custom-build and rigorously-tested Linux kernel called "Oracle Unbreakable Kernel", tight integration with Oracle's hardware and software products including most database applications, and "zero downtime patching" - a feature that enables administrators to update the kernel without a reboot.

items.title: KDu 9-rv3
items.summary: GNU/Linux KDu is a Brazilian desktop Linux distribution based on Ubuntu and KDE neon. It features a customised KDE Plasma desktop and a large collection of software applications for daily and technical use, including office and productivity suites, various maintenance, data recovery and hardware diagnostic utilities, as well as tools for remote access and virtualisation. The distribution is localised into Brazilian Portuguese, inclusive of Brazilian data formats, and is suitable for both new and advanced Linux users.

items.title: ExTiX 261118
items.summary: ExTiX is a desktop Linux distribution and live DVD based on Ubuntu, offering a choice of alternative desktop environments.

items.title: Ultimate 2026.11.18
items.summary: Ultimate Edition, first released in December 2006, was a fork of Ubuntu and Linux Mint though recent versions (starting in 2024) have been based on Arch Linux. The goal of the project is to create a complete, seamlessly integrated, visually stimulating, and easy-to-install operating system. Single-button upgrade is one of several special characteristics of this distribution. Other main features include custom desktop and theme with 3D effects, support for a wide range of networking options, including WiFi and Bluetooth, and integration of many extra applications and package repositories.

items.title: AnduinOS 2.1.0
items.summary: AnduinOS is an Ubuntu-based distribution which provides a GNOME desktop which has been themed and styled to resemble Windows 11. The project provides a smaller ISO file than its parent with each supported language split into a separate ISO. Snap support, which is included in Ubuntu, has been removed from AnduinOS.

items.title: Batocera 20261116
items.summary: Batocera.linux is a minimal distribution dedicated to running retrogaming software. The distribution is able to run on most desktop computers, laptops and several single-board computers, including the Raspberry Pi. batocera.linux can be run from a USB thumb drive or SD card, allowing it to be transferred between computers. batocera.linux is based on RecalboxOS.

items.title: instantOS 2026.11.17
items.summary: instantOS is a lightweight, Arch-based Linux distribution featuring instantWM, a custom-built window manager. It is designed primarily for power users. The distribution comes with a range of custom tools and utilities, such as instantARCH (the official instantOS installer), instantCONF (a settings manager), instantMENU (a general-purpose menu), instantASSIST (a set of useful shortcuts), instantSEARCH (a file search interface based on plocate), instantLAUNCH (an AppImage helper), instantLOCK (a lock screen), instantNOTIFY (a notification centre), instantPASS (a graphical application for pass, t…

items.title: PelandukOS 3.7
items.summary: PelandukOS is a desktop Linux distribution based on Debian's "Testing" branch and featuring the GNOME desktop. It supports installation of extra software in various formats, including the native DEB packages, as well as packages created by AppImage, Flatpak and snap technologies. The distribution uses the Calamares system installer and also includes the Steam launcher (a minimal Steam gaming client with a self-update mechanism that can download the full client) and WPS Office (an all-in-one, AI-powered office suite with MS Office compatibility).

items.title: KolibriOS 0.7.7.0-9261
items.summary: KolibriOS is a tiny open-source operating system with a monolithic preemptive kernel and video drivers for 32-bit x86 architecture computers. KolibriOS is a fork of MenuetOS, written entirely in FASM (assembly language). However, C, C++, Free Pascal, Forth, among other high-level languages and compilers, can also be used in application development. KolibriOS features a rich set of applications that include a word processor, image viewer, graphical editor, web browser, and over 30 games.

items.title: Recalbox 10.1.2
items.summary: Recalbox is a dedicated operating system for running video games on emulated retro and console platforms. Recalbox can also be used to run the Kodi media centre. The distribution's interface is primarily navigated with a console game controller, though keyboard support is available for many functions.

items.title: auryn-docker 0.8.2

A dependency-free Dockerfile parser emits BuildStage nodes, the shared image-keyed `Image` hub (the FROM chain, as resolved:false placeholders) and multi-stage COPY --from edges; a `deploy` enrichment links build stages to the code they package (PACKAGES), recomputes image `resolved` and GCs orphan images. Compose/k8s/Helm/Terraform producers join onto the hub. Depends only on auryn-core.

items.title: auryn-cuda 0.8.2
items.summary: CUDA language plugin for Auryn: a fast tree-sitter-cuda engine. CUDA is a superset of C++, so it reuses the auryn-cpp extraction engine verbatim (namespaces/classes/structs/enums/methods/fields/params, type hierarchy, templates, includes/macros, calls) and adds the CUDA-only graph signals: an `execution_space` property (`__global__`/`__device__`/`__host__`) and a LAUNCHES edge for `kernel >>` launches. A deep libclang/nvcc pass is the planned second phase.

items.title: auryn-csharp 0.8.2

items.title: auryn-cpp 0.8.2

A deep libclang engine (template instantiation, overload resolution, ADL, precise header linking) is the planned second phase.

items.title: auryn-core 0.8.2

items.title: auryn-compose 0.8.2
items.summary: Docker Compose plugin for Auryn (deployment & infrastructure tier, ADR 0007). Parses docker-compose files into Service nodes (RUNS_IMAGE the shared Image hub, DEPENDS_ON other services). A `deploy-compose` enrichment links each service that has both `build:` and `image:` to the Dockerfile stage it builds (`build.target`, else the final stage) with BUILDS_IMAGE, marking the image resolved/internal; the stages come from auryn-docker, so install both. Depends on auryn-core and PyYAML.

items.title: Threat Hunting On The Network: An Active Search for Risks on the Wire
items.summary: All threat hunters are looking for evidence of nefarious activity, hopefully before an incident happens. Threat hunting on the network involves actively searching through packet data for malicious activity. Threat hunting on an endpoint depends more heavily on logs. Think of it as on the wire (or in the air) versus on a host itself. Don’t worry, you don’t have to look through every packet in a pcap file. That would make your head explode!
